text: SAST tools read your source code -- not your running application -- and look for patterns known to be dangerous: string-built SQL queries vulnerable to injection, a weak cryptographic function, a hardcoded secret, unsanitized input flowing into a shell command. Because SAST never executes the application, it can run in seconds against a single pull request's diff, with no test environment and no running server required. That's exactly why it's the first automated check in a shift-left pipeline.

For Python, Bandit is a widely used SAST tool purpose-built for scanning Python source. Semgrep applies the same pattern-matching idea across many languages with an extensible rules engine. Either way, the output is the same shape: a file, a line number, a severity, and a description a developer can act on without further digging.

SAST only looks at code your team wrote. Most real applications pull in far more code than that through dependencies -- packages listed in a requirements file that your project imports but never wrote a line of. Dependency scanning, or software composition analysis, checks those exact pinned versions against public vulnerability databases. pip-audit does this for Python against the Python Packaging Advisory Database; npm audit does the same for Node projects. A project can have flawless code of its own and still ship a serious issue through a vulnerable dependency.

Here's both checks in one real pipeline: checkout the code, set up Python, install dependencies, then run Bandit for static analysis and pip-audit for the dependency check -- all on every pull request, before the application is ever built into a deployable artifact, let alone deployed. These are the cheapest, fastest checks in the whole pipeline, so they run first and most often.

Neither tool is perfect. SAST flags patterns, not confirmed exploits, so some findings are false positives. Dependency scanners can flag a vulnerable function in a package your code never actually calls. Teams that succeed with these tools build a habit of triaging findings quickly, rather than ignoring the tool or treating every finding as a hard blocker -- a tension Lesson 24 tackles head-on when it covers setting gates around real risk instead of noise.
